title: Economical mixed-product disassembly and recovery

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an adaptable industrial system that turns diverse discarded products into reusable components or materials of verified quality at an economically practical cost. It would handle mixed incoming goods whose designs, condition and hazards may differ substantially, including unfamiliar models and worn or damaged items. Its defining advance would be coordinating the whole recovery process across changing products.

Proposed system scope: identify each item, assess its condition, choose a recovery route, plan and execute safe disassembly, sort the outputs and verify their suitability for reuse or downstream processing. It would also decide when to stop, reject an item or redirect it because further recovery would be unsafe or uneconomical. Human supervision and intervention are compatible with this concept; full autonomy is not a completion requirement.

Specialized iPhone disassembly and experimental battery-disassembly systems illustrate parts of this pathway. They also show why separating a product into components is only one stage: a broader capability must connect those operations to usable outputs, downstream recovery and facility economics.

significance.text: Conditional impact assessment: if such systems achieved reliable recovery, output quality and economic performance across diverse product streams, they could make a much broader range of discarded complex goods practical production inputs. The substantial enabling advance would be extending recovery beyond facilities tailored to narrow product streams, while retaining viable operating costs as designs and incoming conditions change.

The direct technical opportunity includes both component reuse and material recovery. The battery study describes condition-dependent routes toward second-life use or raw-material recovery, while Apple describes retrieving and sorting components containing high-quality materials. Preserving usable components could retain value that would otherwise require further processing to recover as raw materials, although these sources do not quantify that advantage across mixed products.

Conditional downstream possibilities include less demand for newly extracted materials and lower environmental burdens. Those benefits would depend on collection, energy use, downstream conversion, demand for recovered outputs and whether those outputs actually substitute for newly produced inputs. Economic disassembly alone would not establish a net lifecycle benefit. The concept also does not imply that every material or bond can be economically recovered, that all discarded goods can circulate indefinitely, or that success within several product families establishes universal recoverability.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target breakthrough is dependable integration of identification, condition assessment, planning, safe physical operations, routing and quality assurance under substantial product variability, with viable economics across the complete process. The supplied evidence establishes relevant specialized achievements and continuing battery-disassembly challenges. It does not establish that this broader capability is absent everywhere in industry.

A concrete engineering barrier is coping with uncertainty in the object being handled. The battery study identifies variations in geometry and joining techniques, together with wear, contamination and unknown damage, as conditions that can exceed the robustness of perception-driven automation. Recognizing an item does not by itself establish its internal condition or make the next operation safe. Perception, planning and execution must remain coordinated when the actual product differs from the expected configuration.

Robustness must also be reconciled with throughput, labor requirements and cost. The battery study identifies automation level, system robustness and economic efficiency as interacting conditions for commercial viability, and presents hybrid human–AI operation as a realistic development path. Its finding that people were essential to the demonstrated system does not prove that every future implementation must require the same interventions.

Proposed additional requirements for the broader concept are reliable sorting, downstream output-quality verification and economically informed decisions about rejection or redirection. A system must distinguish a technically possible separation from one that yields a useful output at an acceptable total cost. The supplied evidence does not determine which specific materials or bonds would remain uneconomical, or establish the cost of meeting these requirements across mixed product families.

current_state.text: On April 19, 2018, Apple reported that its Daisy robot could disassemble nine versions of iPhone at up to 200 devices per hour, removing and sorting components for recycling. These are company-reported compatibility and maximum-rate figures for a known product family. The supplied release does not establish independently measured sustained throughput, comparative total economics or an end-to-end demonstration of downstream recovery from mixed products.

The study published on May 25, 2026, “Advancing sustainable electromobility: development and practical assessment of an AI-Assisted Semi-Automated battery disassembly system,” reports an integrated demonstrator combining perception and robotic operations. Its experimental validation used modular battery dummies rather than real end-of-life batteries, in controlled laboratory conditions and with limited configurations. This supports feasibility of the tested integration, while leaving transfer to damaged, variable real-world battery systems unestablished by those experiments.

Human supervision, validation and intervention were essential to maintaining stability in the battery demonstrator, particularly where perception, planning and execution interacted. The authors identify further economic and operational work needed for industrial scaling. Neither this result nor Apple's reported Daisy capability demonstrates economical end-to-end recovery across mixed real-world product streams; that conclusion describes the scope of these two results rather than the entire industry's capabilities.

Evidence boundary: the supplied review reports complete retained HTML for both sources and grounds the battery study's experimental limitations in its prose. Figures were not visually inspected in that review, so no additional conclusions about the apparatus or its performance are drawn from them here. The dated results remain informative, but the supplied materials contain no freshness assessment establishing whether subsequent work had demonstrated the broader capability by November 1, 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently operated facilities would process representative, unsorted incoming streams spanning several complex product families and manufacturers, including damaged products and models not used during development. Before testing, evaluators would define the operating envelope, incoming-stream composition, test duration and economic and recovery thresholds. These are proposed evaluation choices, not established completion standards.
completion_criteria.label: Independent facilities process representative unsorted streams including unseen, damaged products

completion_criteria.text: Proposed accounting would include every incoming item, including rejected or redirected goods, and follow outputs through downstream processing. Measurements would cover recovery by mass, material or component quality, safety, labor and intervention, throughput, total cost and lifecycle impacts. This would prevent high disassembly rates or selective acceptance of easy products from standing in for useful recovery across the declared stream.
completion_criteria.label: Every incoming item and downstream output receives full recovery accounting

completion_criteria.text: A convincing proposed outcome would demonstrate economical operation at scale and materially more usable recovery than credible alternatives evaluated under the same accounting boundaries. Human-assisted operation could qualify if its labor, interventions and costs were included. Repetition across independent facilities and additional representative batches would strengthen reproducibility and show how performance changes with incoming conditions.
completion_criteria.label: Economical operation at scale yields more usable recovery than alternatives

completion_criteria.text: The demonstrated capability would remain bounded by the tested product families, conditions, hazards, throughput and downstream routes. Reporting failures, exclusions and uneconomical cases would be part of establishing those practical boundaries. Finite demonstrations could establish substantial breadth and transfer to unseen models within that envelope, but could not establish literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Reported capability boundaries identify failures, exclusions and uneconomical cases

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison with IND-01, “General-purpose, rapidly reconfigurable production”: both concepts concern adaptable physical operations across changing products. IND-01 centers on production; IND-04 centers on recovering value from existing goods whose condition and construction may be uncertain. Reconfigurable tools and planning could contribute to both, while recovery adds incoming-condition assessment, recovery routing and downstream output-quality requirements.

Roster-based comparison with IND-02, “Production-time qualification of individual critical parts”: both involve verifying whether an individual output is fit for use. Recovered components may require qualification before reuse, but IND-04 also encompasses identifying and disassembling incoming goods, sorting materials and achieving viable recovery economics. It does not itself establish that a recovered critical part meets all requirements for its intended application.

Roster-based comparison with IND-03, “A predictive and testable science of supply-network cascade containment”: recovery could conditionally provide additional sources of components or materials, potentially affecting supply-network resilience. IND-04 would not by itself predict cascades or establish how to contain them. Those effects would depend on the availability, timing, quality and substitutability of recovered outputs.

Roster-based comparison with IND-05, “Transferable prediction and prevention of work-related human performance risk”: human-assisted recovery creates an overlap around supervision, intervention and safe work. IND-04 seeks a functioning recovery process and must account for its human demands; IND-05 concerns transferable prediction and prevention of human performance risk. Successful recovery operations would not alone validate that broader predictive capability.

Roster-based comparison with IND-06, “Transferable safety constraints built into socio-technical systems”: handling damaged or hazardous products requires safety constraints that remain effective as items and operations change. Such constraints could support IND-04, while IND-06 addresses their transfer across socio-technical settings more broadly. Safe performance in a bounded recovery facility would provide evidence within that setting, rather than establish general transferability.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not determine whether any other industrial system had achieved the broader mixed-product capability by November 1, 2026; no freshness assessment was supplied.
Sustained independently measured Daisy throughput, total recovery economics and downstream recovery performance are not established by the supplied Apple release.
The battery demonstrator's performance on real end-of-life batteries, broader configurations and industrial-scale operations remains unestablished by its dummy-based laboratory validation.
The materials, bonds and incoming conditions that would make recovery unsafe or uneconomical, and the applicable decision thresholds, remain unspecified.
Representative stream composition, test duration, operating scale and quantitative economic, safety, quality and lifecycle success thresholds remain proposed design choices to be defined.
The supplied review did not visually inspect figures; no additional apparatus or performance findings have been inferred from them.
Related-concept comparisons rely on the supplied roster titles because detailed records for those concepts were not provided.

brief.title: Affordable recovery of parts from mixed discarded goods
possible: Discarded phones, batteries and other complex goods could supply reusable parts and materials, even when they arrive mixed together, worn or damaged. Recovery facilities could handle unfamiliar models at a practical cost.

A system would identify each item, assess its condition, take it apart safely and check the recovered outputs. It would also decide when to stop or redirect an item. People could supervise and intervene.
why: Manufacturers could draw useful inputs from a broader range of discarded goods. Recovery facilities could adapt as product designs change, extending beyond narrowly tailored recycling operations.
Keeping usable components intact could preserve value that would otherwise require further processing to recover as raw materials.

sources.showed: Apple reported that its Daisy robot could take apart several iPhone models and sort their components for recycling.
sources.quote: Daisy can take apart up to 200 iPhone devices per hour.
sources.cited_for: Daisy demonstrates specialized disassembly and sorting within a known product family.
sources.not_established: The report does not establish sustained performance or economical recovery across mixed products.

sources.who: Gerald Bräunig and colleagues at Chemnitz University of Technology
sources.showed: The researchers combined camera-based recognition, robotic operations and human supervision in a battery-disassembly demonstrator. Tests used dummy batteries in controlled laboratory conditions.
sources.quote:
Experimental validation demonstrates successful robotic unscrewing rates of 
up to 98.8% and reliable execution of integrated disassembly sequences in most test cases.
sources.cited_for: The experiments demonstrate coordinated disassembly and the importance of human intervention in the tested system.
sources.not_established: The tests do not establish safe, economical operation on damaged, used batteries at industrial scale.

shown: Apple has reported automated disassembly and sorting for a known phone family. The Chemnitz team demonstrated coordinated battery-disassembly tasks using laboratory dummies, with human supervision essential to stable operation.
missing: Dependable coordination from identification through recovery must be demonstrated across mixed, unfamiliar and damaged products.
Recovered parts and materials need quality checks and tracking through subsequent processing.
The complete process must work at a viable cost, including labor, interventions and rejected items.
Safe, economical decisions about stopping or redirecting difficult items remain to be demonstrated across varied products.

milestones.label: Independent facilities handle mixed, unfamiliar and damaged products
milestones.explanation: Independent facilities would process representative unsorted goods from several product families and manufacturers, including unfamiliar and damaged models. This would test adaptability under agreed conditions.

milestones.label: Every item and recovered output is accounted for
milestones.explanation: Accounting would track all inputs and outputs through further processing, covering quality, safety, labor, processing rate, cost and environmental effects. This would distinguish useful recovery from simply taking products apart.

milestones.label: Economical recovery at scale outperforms credible alternatives
milestones.explanation: Operation at scale would yield materially more usable recovery than credible alternatives under matching accounting rules, including human assistance costs. Repeated results across facilities and batches would establish reliability.

milestones.label: Failures, exclusions and uneconomical cases define capability limits
milestones.explanation: Results would identify failures and exclusions across tested products, hazards, conditions and recovery routes. This would establish where the system works and where recovery remains unsafe or uneconomical.

uncertain: Which materials, bonds and damage conditions would make recovery unsafe or too costly?
What mix of products, operating scale and success thresholds would constitute a convincing demonstration?
Would recovered outputs replace newly produced inputs enough to reduce overall environmental harm?

page.title: Mixed-product robotic disassembly and recovery
page.definition: A reconfigurable system disassembles discarded products from multiple product families and supplies recovered components or materials for reuse or recycling, with receipts covering total recovery costs. Identification, condition assessment, routing, disassembly, sorting and output acceptance are linked; people may supervise and intervene.

goal.need: Only 22.3% of electronic-waste mass generated globally in 2022 was documented as formally collected and recycled. Fraunhofer’s iDEAR programme targets extraction of reusable components and material fractions, with disassembly depth chosen using secondary-material prices and product valuations.

figures.caption: Global electronic-waste flows in 2022
figures.note: These are waste-management flows, not estimates of what robotic disassembly could recover.

completion.title: A mixed-product recovery system covers its full costs while supplying accepted recovered outputs.
completion.criterion: An operating reconfigurable system processes a declared stream spanning at least two product families, including models not used during development and worn or damaged items. It assesses condition, chooses disassembly or rejection routes, separates and sorts outputs, and supplies components or materials meeting recipients’ acceptance specifications. Receipts from recovered outputs and treatment services cover collection, amortised capital, labour, energy, maintenance, rejected items and downstream treatment over the demonstrated operating period. Human assistance is allowed and costed.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional test because no external completion criterion covering the combined capability was located.
completion.basis: Searches of EN 45555’s published scope, NIST manipulation benchmarks and ROB4GREEN’s call requirements found no common test combining product diversity, accepted recovered outputs and whole-process economics. Receipts covering costs is the narrow Atlas interpretation of Fraunhofer’s cost-effective recovery objective. The external maturity gates below do not establish economic success.

milestones.title: Robotic disassembly technology passes laboratory validation (TRL 4).
milestones.criterion: Disassembly technology is validated in the laboratory, the Commission’s technology readiness level 4 criterion. Bräunig et al., published on 25 May 2026, report 125 successful AI-guided unscrewing attempts out of 150 on a flat screw pattern. Their battery demonstrators used modular dummies under human supervision. This supports laboratory disassembly subsystems; it does not validate downstream material recovery or establish a TRL for the complete capability.
milestones.set_by: European Commission, Horizon 2020 General Annex G; a generic maturity definition applied here to disassembly technology.

milestones.title: A disassembly-and-recovery prototype is demonstrated in a relevant industrial environment (TRL 6).
milestones.criterion: The prototype is demonstrated in an industrially relevant environment, corresponding to TRL 6. ROB4GREEN requires this deployment before operational validation. ReconCycle’s report, updated on 23 May 2025, describes a workcell handling heat cost allocators and smoke detectors, with engineer-led reconfiguration between device types and autonomous adaptation between models within a category. It provides no test sample size or whole-process cost result and does not establish this gate for the complete recovery chain.
milestones.set_by: Horizon Europe ROB4GREEN consortium, Open Call 1 Technical Description, section 5.1.2; TRL 6 terminology follows the European Commission’s generic definition.
milestones.threshold_quote: deployment of a demonstrator of the system prototype in relevant environment

milestones.title: A disassembly-and-recovery prototype is demonstrated in an operational environment (TRL 7).
milestones.criterion: An integrated prototype is demonstrated in an operational environment, the ROB4GREEN TRL 7 gate. Apple reported nine iPhone models and a maximum rate of 200 devices per hour on 19 April 2018. Circu Li-ion’s report, updated on 11 March 2025, reports 80 battery packs processed and a line handling different assemblies and brands. These developer reports are not peer reviewed; neither establishes integrated recovery quality and economics across mixed product families.
milestones.set_by: Horizon Europe ROB4GREEN consortium, Open Call 1 Technical Description, section 5.1.3; a programme prototype-validation requirement.
milestones.threshold_quote: system prototype demonstration in an operational environment (TRL7).

milestones.title: A mixed-product disassembly-and-recovery system is complete and qualified (TRL 8).
milestones.criterion: The complete disassembly-and-recovery system is qualified, corresponding to TRL 8. This gate concerns the complete system within its declared operating envelope. The Commission’s generic definition supplies no disassembly-specific qualification protocol, recovered-output grade or economic threshold. No qualification result covering the combined capability was located.
milestones.set_by: European Commission, Horizon 2020 General Annex G; a generic system-maturity definition, not a disassembly-specific acceptance standard.

not_found: No common completion test for mixed-product recovery quality and whole-process economics was found in searches of CEN/NEN, NIST and EU robotics programmes.
The full EN 45555 standard was not accessed; its published scope was available.
No demonstration combining unfamiliar or damaged products, accepted recovered outputs and full cost recovery across mixed product families was located.
No application-specific qualification protocol or qualification result for the complete mixed-product recovery system was located.
No independently measured sustained Daisy throughput or comparative total recovery economics was located.

results.finding: Apple reports Daisy can disassemble nine iPhone models at up to 200 devices per hour; test sample size is not reported.
results.detail: The release describes one product family and does not establish an operational demonstration of the complete recovery chain, including output acceptance and economics.
results.quote: Daisy can take apart up to 200 iPhone devices per hour, removing and sorting components, so that Apple can recover materials that traditional recyclers can’t — and at a higher quality.

results.finding: AI-guided robotic unscrewing succeeded in 125 of 150 attempts on a flat screw pattern.
results.detail: The controlled tests support laboratory validation of a disassembly subsystem. The battery demonstrators used modular dummies; the study does not validate downstream recovery or establish a TRL for the complete capability.
results.quote:
A total of 150 unscrewing attempts were consequently conducted 
with 125 being successful, 15 not being recognized by the 
AI, and 10 not being close enough to the actual position.

results.finding: Robotic smoke-detector battery extraction succeeded in 18 of 20 attempts.
results.detail: Tests assumed prior clamping, housing cutting and battery positioning. Two failures required manual disassembly. The report describes an experimental workcell but does not explicitly identify the extraction test as laboratory validation or assign it a TRL.
results.quote: Out of 20 battery removal attempts, 18 were successful.

results.finding: ADIR demonstrator processed nearly 2,000 items in field tests at a recycling plant.
results.detail: The line handled mobile phones and printed circuit boards, including boards from servers. The report does not establish the complete recovery chain across multiple product families or provide total recovery cost receipts.
results.quote: In field tests with the ADIR demonstrator nearly 2000 items have been processed, new sorting fractions with high enrichment of target metals were generated and recovery rates of > 95 % for target elements were shown.

results.finding: Hiro Robotics’ TV and monitor disassembly system: sample size not reported; adaptable to process up to 90 monitors per hour.
results.detail: The source describes a system operating at a recycling plant with human sorting, but does not establish integrated recovery quality and total recovery costs across mixed product families. The 90-per-hour figure is an adaptation capacity, not a reported measured throughput.
results.quote: This modular approach can be adapted to process up to 90 monitors per hour, significantly reducing processing time, improving efficiency, and reducing operating costs.

results.finding: Apple reports Daisy can disassemble 36 iPhone models; the number of devices tested is not stated.
results.detail: The page reports 200 devices disassembled per hour but does not establish an integrated operational prototype across product families, recovery quality, or total recovery costs.
results.quote: Our robot Daisy can disassemble 36 iPhone models into discrete parts, so we can recover and recycle more materials.
